verdict: ROAS is up sharply, but purchase volume is still too thin to call a trend.
narrative: This period your Meta ads returned $3.30 for every $1.00 spent — a 158% jump in return on ad spend week-over-week — driven primarily by your top campaign, which absorbed $840 of the $1,490 in total spend. That efficiency gain came without increasing budget, meaning the targeting is working harder, not just spending more. Purchase volume, however, sits at 21 transactions over 28 days, and the most recent days show purchases flatlining rather than accelerating, so the ROAS headline is promising but not yet reliable at this volume. Site traffic rose over 20% week-over-week while purchases held flat, which points to a conversion gap on the site itself — we're monitoring this closely and the funnel test and UTM tracking are set to close out by August 31. Next period, expect sharper visibility into where site visitors are dropping off, along with new creative entering rotation once the overdue content shoot is resolved.

highlights.phrase: return on ad spend over the last 28 days, up 158% from the prior 7-day period
purchases driven by Meta ads this period — volume is growing but still building
actions taken on your Google Business Profile this period — calls, directions, and site clicks

watch_item.issue: Site traffic rose 21% this week but purchases did not follow, pointing to a conversion gap rather than a reach problem.
watch_item.fix: The funnel test closes and conversion tracking goes fully live by August 31, which will show exactly where visitors are dropping off so we can act on it.
